name: Freshdesk
subcategory: help desks, live chat and support knowledge
tagline: Manage tickets from email and a web form with priorities, owners, and a help center
verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Freshdesk, manage tickets from email and a web form with priorities, owners, and a help center. The hard boundary is omnichannel features, automations, marketplace, reporting, and freshworks ecosystem, plus channel integrations and support operations.
coreLoopDIY: Receive customer messages from email and a web form, manage tickets with priorities and owners, reply from one shared inbox, publish a help center, and retain searchable conversation history.
whatYouLose: omnichannel features, automations, marketplace, reporting, and Freshworks ecosystem
ongoingBurden: message delivery, webhooks, threading, identity, permissions, attachments, notifications, spam, search, uptime, and retention
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Freshdesk because support software survives because missing or misrouting one customer message is expensive and every channel behaves differently. The recurring cost buys message delivery, webhooks, threading, identity, permissions, attachments, notifications, spam, search, uptime, and retention, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Chatwoot
priorArt.desc: Mature open-source customer engagement and shared-inbox platform.

alternatives.name: Chatwoot
alternatives.desc: A proper support inbox with chat, email and a help center; free software, billable server chores.

alternatives.name: Frappe Helpdesk
alternatives.desc: Tickets, SLAs and a knowledge base in a clean Frappe shell; the five-minute installer still leaves you the pager.

alternatives.name: osTicket
alternatives.desc: Email and web forms become assigned tickets; dated, dependable and very much your PHP server.

alternatives.name: Zammad
alternatives.desc: A serious ticket desk with email, chat, SLAs and a knowledge base; setup is the first ticket.

rejectedAlternatives.name: FreeScout
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The shared inbox is free, but its knowledge base is a paid module, so it misses the stated job.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Growth plan and a small-team shared inbox DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Freshdesk in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, WebSockets, and Docker Compose; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: receive customer messages from email and a web form, manage tickets with priorities and owners, reply from one shared inbox, publish a help center, and retain searchable conversation history.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Implement one workspace, agents, contacts, inboxes, conversations, messages, labels, and assignment.
Provide a website chat widget with reconnect, unread counts, file limits, and clear availability state.
Create a shared inbox with filters, collision warnings, notes, canned replies, and searchable history.
Add email notifications, browser notifications, and an immutable assignment and status log.
Implement spam controls, attachment scanning hooks, retention settings, export, and contact deletion.
Ship Docker Compose, backups, health checks, migrations, and a documented admin recovery flow.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out many social and messaging channels.
Deliberately leave out AI agents trained on proprietary support data.
Deliberately leave out enterprise workforce management, SSO, and compliance.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
